intent: The draggable, keyboard-operable divider between two panels of a ResizablePanelGroup.
typical_uses: The divider between two adjacent panels, optionally with a visible grip

dont_use_when.situation: A static dividing line that nobody drags

invariants.text: The handle's `aria-orientation` describes the drawn line, which is the opposite of the group's `orientation`: `vertical` in a horizontal group and `horizontal` in a vertical one. resizable.module.css keys the handle's geometry and the grip's 90 degree rotation on it.

A focused handle resizes its neighbours with the arrow keys along the group's axis and with Home and End, Enter collapses or expands the panel before the handle when it is `collapsible`, and F6 moves focus to the group's next handle (Shift+F6 to the previous). Double-clicking resets the first adjoining panel that has a `defaultSize` to it, unless `disableDoubleClick` is set; with no `defaultSize` on either it does nothing.
A `disabled` handle cannot be used to resize its neighbouring panels, is removed from the tab order and carries `aria-disabled`; its panels can still change size when another handle moves them.

anti_patterns.dont: Put an icon or text inside the handle as children
anti_patterns.do_instead: Set `withHandle` for the kit's grip; the handle renders no consumer children

a11y.by: the primitive's Separator (role="separator", aria-orientation, aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, aria-controls, tabIndex 0 unless disabled, and arrow, Home, End and Enter keyboard resizing), plus resizable.test.tsx asserting role separator and aria-orientation vertical in a horizontal group and horizontal in a vertical one

elementRef.states: elementRef is a ref to the handle's div element
elementRef.because: `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` is a union of a ref object and a callback function - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style is a plain style object applied inline to the handle's div
style.because: `CSSProperties` is React's style object type, which the compiler leaves to tsc. The library sets `flex-grow` and `flex-shrink` after it, so those two cannot be overridden; the kit's own styling goes through resizable.module.css.

unexposed_parts.reason: A div styled by resizable.module.css's `.grip`, holding a vertical grip icon, rendered only when `withHandle` is set; it is not a component of its own.

good.title: A handle with a visible grip

bad.title: A custom icon passed as children
bad.why: The handle renders only the kit's grip; the icon never appears.

elementRef.description: TS: Ref<HTMLDivElement> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. elementRef is a ref to the handle's div element. `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` is a union of a ref object and a callback function - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.
